questions.question: Minimum Support Prices are decided by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)** is responsible for approving the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for various crops in India.
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the government to ensure **agricultural producers are protected against any sharp fall in farm prices.**
 
• The CCEA takes decisions based on the recommendations of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).**
 
• MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops and an additional bonus for some crops in certain cases.
 
• The primary objective of MSP is to ensure a remunerative price to farmers and encourage them to adopt modern farming practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP):**

 
 
• CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.
 
• It recommends MSPs for crops based on factors like cost of production, demand-supply balance, and market price trends.
 
 
 
• **Factors Considered for MSP:**
 
 
• Cost of cultivation, including inputs like seeds, fertilizers, and labor.
 
• Trends in domestic and international market prices.
 
• Parity between crops and ensuring fair returns to farmers.
 
 
 
• **Mandated Crops under MSP:**
 
 
• Includes cereals (wheat, rice, maize, etc.), pulses (tur, moong, urad), oilseeds (soybean, mustard, groundnut), and commercial crops (cotton, sugarcane).
 
 
 
• **Role of MSP in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Encourages farmers to grow particular crops to meet food security needs.
 
• Acts as a safety net for farmers during market price fluctuations.
 
• Helps stabilize the rural economy and reduce farmer distress.

questions.question: Which of the following National Waterways (NW) connects Sadiya-Dhubri in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NW-2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• National Waterway 2 (NW-2) specifically designates the Brahmaputra River stretch between Sadiya and Dhubri in Assam.
 
• This vital waterway spans approximately 891 kilometers.
 
• It serves as a crucial artery for inland water transport in the region.
 
• It plays a significant role in facilitating the movement of both goods and passengers, connecting various towns and districts within Assam.
 
• This waterway is not only important for intra-state trade but also holds potential for regional connectivity with neighboring countries.
 
• The development of NW-2 has been a focus for enhancing multimodal transport options in the Northeast.
 
• This aims to reduce reliance on road and rail for certain types of cargo.
 
• Its navigability is key to unlocking economic opportunities along the riverine areas of Assam.

questions.question: When was the Protection of Human Rights Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Protection of Human Rights Act** was enacted in India in **1993** to provide for the establishment of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC).
 
• The Act aims to protect and promote human rights in accordance with the Constitution of India and international human rights instruments.
 
• The **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** was constituted under this Act as an independent statutory body.
 
• The Act also provides for the formation of **State Human Rights Commissions** to address human rights issues at the state level.
 
• The Act defines "human rights" as rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):**

 
 
• Established in October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
 
• It consists of a Chairperson and other members appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Commission investigates complaints of human rights violations and provides recommendations to the government.
 
 
 
• **State Human Rights Commissions:**
 
 
• Each state in India can establish its own Human Rights Commission under the Act.
 
• These bodies address human rights issues specific to their respective states.
 
 
 
• **International Human Rights Instruments:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to major human rights treaties such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR).
 
• The Protection of Human Rights Act aligns with international standards to safeguard human rights.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the Act:**
 
 
• The Act has been amended several times to strengthen the functioning of NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions.
 
• The latest amendment was made in 2019 to include changes in the composition and tenure of members.

questions.question: Who among the following was/were NOT part of the Santhal Rebellion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tana Bhagats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56)** was led by tribal leaders **Sidhu, Kanho, Chand, and Bhairav Murmu** to resist British colonial oppression and exploitation by landlords and moneylenders.
 
• The rebellion primarily took place in the **Rajmahal Hills** of present-day Jharkhand, where the Santhal tribes united against oppressive policies.
 
• Tana Bhagats, a tribal group from the Oraon community, were not part of the Santhal Rebellion. They emerged later in 1914, as followers of Mahatma Gandhi's non-violent principles.
 
• The Santhal Rebellion was one of the significant tribal uprisings against British rule, marked by violent resistance to reclaim tribal autonomy and land rights.
 
• The rebellion was ultimately crushed by the British forces, but it led to the creation of the Santhal Pargana district in 1856 to address tribal grievances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santhal Rebellion (1855-56):**

 
 
• Also known as the Hul Rebellion, it was a tribal uprising led by the Santhal community against British rule and exploitation by zamindars and moneylenders.
 
• The rebellion marked a significant resistance movement before the Indian Revolt of 1857.
 
 
 
• **Tana Bhagats Movement (1914):**
 
 
• Founded by Jatra Oraon, the Tana Bhagats were a tribal reformist group inspired by Gandhian ideals of non-violence and self-purification.
 
• They opposed British taxes and participated in the Civil Disobedience Movement.
 
 
 
• **Sidhu and Kanho Murmu:**
 
 
• They were the key leaders of the Santhal Rebellion, who mobilized thousands of tribal people in the fight against colonial oppression.
 
• Their leadership remains a symbol of tribal resistance in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Santhal Rebellion:**
 
 
• It highlighted the grievances of tribal communities under British rule, especially regarding land alienation and exploitation.
 
• It led to administrative changes, including the establishment of the Santhal Pargana district.

questions.question: Which of the following is non-agro based industry ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leather industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Leather industry** is classified as a non-agro based industry as it primarily relies on raw materials like animal hides and skins, not agricultural crops.
 
• It is one of India's oldest manufacturing industries, contributing significantly to exports and employment, especially in small and medium enterprises.
 
• This industry involves processes like tanning, finishing, and manufacturing leather goods such as footwear, belts, and bags.
 
• India is one of the top leather-producing countries globally, with key production hubs in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal.
 
• The leather industry also plays a vital role in sustainability through initiatives like waste reduction and eco-friendly tanning methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agro-based industries** are industries that depend directly on agricultural raw materials, such as sugar, jute, and tobacco.
 
• **Sugar industry**: Processes sugarcane into sugar and other by-products like molasses and ethanol.
 
• **Tobacco industry**: Uses tobacco leaves for manufacturing products such as cigarettes and chewing tobacco.
 
• **Jute industry**: Relies on jute fiber for making ropes, sacks, and other products.
 
• **Leather processing**: Involves chemical treatments like tanning to make animal hides durable and suitable for product manufacturing.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of standing committees cannot be classified into their respective categories?

options.text: Committees Relating to the Day-to-Day Business of the House: Rules Committee
Committees to Scrutinise and Control: Committee on Absence of Members from Sittings of the House

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: Committees to Scrutinise and Control - Committee on Absence of Members from Sittings of the House**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Committee on Absence of Members from Sittings of the House** does not fall under the "Committees to Scrutinise and Control" category. Instead, it is categorized as a "Housekeeping Committee."
 
• "Committees to Scrutinise and Control" include committees like the **Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings**, which focus on ensuring financial accountability and oversight.
 
• The **Committee on Absence of Members** primarily deals with granting leave of absence to members and does not have a scrutinizing or controlling mandate.
 
• The classification of parliamentary committees in India is based on their functions, such as financial control, inquiry, or day-to-day business management.
 
• Incorrect categorization of committees undermines their purpose, which is to ensure smooth legislative functioning and accountability in parliamentary proceedings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Categories of Standing Committees:**

 
 
• **Financial Committees:** Includes the Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings.
 
• **Committees to Inquire:** Includes the Ethics Committee and Committee on Privileges.
 
• **Committees Relating to Day-to-Day Business:** Includes the Business Advisory Committee, Rules Committee, and Committee on Absence of Members from Sittings of the House.
 
• **Committees to Scrutinise and Control:** Includes committees like Public Accounts and Estimates Committees.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• Applies to the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
• Empowers district and regional councils to make laws, but these require the Governor's assent.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor has the authority to reorganize autonomous districts and regions in tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule.
 
• The Governor plays a supervisory role to ensure that tribal governance aligns with constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Fifth Schedule:**
 
 
• The Fifth Schedule deals with scheduled areas and tribes outside the northeastern states and does not include district councils.
 
• It focuses on the administration and welfare of scheduled tribes through Tribes Advisory Councils.

questions.question: Which one of the following is listed in the Ain-i Akbari as one of the 'Indian sciences' prescribed by Akbar for scholars to learn at school?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jyotisha**, or Indian astrology, was listed as one of the 'Indian sciences' in the **Ain-i Akbari**, written by Abu'l-Fazl during Emperor Akbar's reign.
 
• It is an ancient Indian system of astronomy and astrology used to calculate auspicious timings (muhurta) for various activities.
 
• The Ain-i Akbari emphasizes Akbar's interest in blending Indian and Persian cultural knowledge, including sciences like Jyotisha.
 
• Jyotisha was considered a scholarly subject and included in the curriculum for students at schools (madrasas) during Akbar's era.
 
• Akbar's patronage of Indian sciences reflects his efforts to foster intellectual growth and cultural synthesis in his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ain-i Akbari**

 
 
• It is a 16th-century Persian text written by Akbar's court historian Abu'l-Fazl.
 
• The text is part of the larger work Akbarnama and serves as an administrative, cultural, and social record of Akbar's empire.
 
• The Ain-i Akbari includes details on governance, revenue systems, military organization, and cultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Indian Sciences in Ain-i Akbari**
 
 
• Ain-i Akbari mentions several Indian sciences, including Ayurveda, Jyotisha (astrology), Ganita (mathematics), and Vyakarana (grammar).
 
• These sciences were integrated into the education system of Akbar's time to promote intellectual diversity.
 
 
 
• **Jyotisha's Significance**
 
 
• Jyotisha combines astronomy and astrology to calculate planetary movements and their influence on human life.
 
• It was historically used to determine auspicious dates for events like marriages, coronations, and religious ceremonies.
 
• Jyotisha is one of the six Vedangas or auxiliary disciplines linked to the Vedas, showcasing its ancient roots.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Educational Reforms**
 
 
• Akbar established schools and madrasas that taught a blend of Indian and Persian sciences.
 
• His interest in Indian knowledge systems reflects his policy of Sulh-i-Kul (universal peace) and cultural inclusivity.

questions.question: Where is Kandariya Mahadev Temple situated ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khajuraho**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kandariya Mahadev Temple is situated in **Khajuraho**, Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It is the **largest and most ornate Hindu temple** in the Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
 
• This temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and was built during the reign of the Chandela dynasty, around the **11th century CE**.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **Nagara-style architecture**, which features intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• Kandariya Mahadev Temple is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** of Khajuraho, known for its stunning depiction of art and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara-style Architecture:**

 
 
• A style of temple architecture primarily found in **North India**.
 
• Characterized by a **shikhara (spire)** that rises vertically and intricate carvings depicting deities, mythical creatures, and daily life.
 
 
 
• **Chandela Dynasty:**
 
 
• Rulers who established the **Khajuraho Group of Monuments** between the 9th and 13th centuries.
 
• The dynasty is known for its contribution to art, architecture, and temple-building.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1986**.
 
• It includes **22 surviving temples** out of the original 85, showcasing a blend of Hindu and Jain architectural styles.
 
 
 
• **Erotic Sculptures:**
 
 
• The temples of Khajuraho are famous for their **erotic sculptures**, which symbolize the celebration of love, life, and divinity.
 
• These carvings are believed to depict the **Kama Sutra** and reflect the liberal ethos of medieval Indian society.

questions.question: Who was the last Viceroy and the first Governor General of independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Mountbatten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lord Louis Mountbatten** was the last Viceroy of British India and the first Governor-General of independent India.
 
• He served as the Viceroy from **February 1947 to August 1947** and oversaw the partition of India into two nations, India and Pakistan.
 
• After India's independence on 15 August 1947, Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of India and held this position until **June 1948**.
 
• Mountbatten was the only British Governor-General of independent India, after which the role was assumed by Indian leaders starting with **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari** in 1948.
 
• Mountbatten's tenure was marked by significant events, including the communal violence during partition and the accession of princely states to the Indian Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Viceroy of India:**

 
 
• The Viceroy was the head of the British administration in India, representing the British Crown.
 
• The position was established in 1858 after the abolition of the East India Company's rule and continued until 1947.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General of India:**
 
 
• The Governor-General was originally the head of the British administration in India before the creation of the Viceroy position in 1858.
 
• Post-independence, the Governor-General became the representative of the British monarch in India until India became a republic in 1950.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India:**
 
 
• The partition was a significant event in Indian history, leading to the creation of two independent nations, India and Pakistan, on 15 August 1947.
 
• It resulted in massive communal violence, displacement, and loss of lives, affecting millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari:**
 
 
• He was the first and only Indian Governor-General of independent India, serving from June 1948 to January 1950.
 
• He played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement and was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: What is the highest ever medal tally achieved by India at Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**101**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India achieved its highest-ever medal tally of **101 medals** at the **2010 Commonwealth Games** held in Delhi, India.
 
• This tally included **39 gold, 26 silver, and 36 bronze medals**, showcasing India's best performance in the history of the Commonwealth Games.
 
• The 2010 Commonwealth Games was the **19th edition** of the event and marked the first time India hosted the games.
 
• India ranked **second** in the medal tally, with Australia finishing first and England in third place.
 
• Sports such as wrestling, shooting, and athletics were key contributors to India's success in the 2010 edition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonwealth Games Overview:**

 
 
• The Commonwealth Games is a multi-sport event held every four years involving athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations.
 
• It was first held in 1930 as the British Empire Games in Hamilton, Canada.
 
• India has been participating in the Commonwealth Games since 1934 and has consistently improved its performance over the years.
 
 
 
• **Highlights of the 2010 Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• Wrestler Sushil Kumar, shooter Gagan Narang, and boxer Vijender Singh were among the standout performers for India.
 
• India's performance in shooting and wrestling played a significant role in achieving the record-breaking medal tally.
 
• The event witnessed participation from 71 nations and territories.
 
 
 
• **India's Best Performances in Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• India's second-best performance occurred during the 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games, where the country secured 66 medals.
 
• India has consistently performed well in sports like shooting, wrestling, weightlifting, and badminton.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 2010 Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• The 2010 Games helped India establish itself as a major sporting nation in the Commonwealth.
 
• It also highlighted India's organizational capabilities, despite challenges in preparation and controversies.

questions.question: Which forest is included in the Palamu Tiger Reserve?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Betla National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Betla National Park is an integral part of the **Palamu Tiger Reserve**, located in Jharkhand, India.
 
• It was one of the first tiger reserves in India to be included under the **Project Tiger initiative** in 1973.
 
• The park is known for its **diverse wildlife**, including tigers, elephants, leopards, and various species of deer and birds.
 
• Spanning across **1,026 sq. km**, Betla National Park comprises dense forests, grasslands, and scenic landscapes.
 
• The park's name "Betla" is an acronym for **Bison, Elephant, Tiger, Leopard, and Axis-axis (chital)**, reflecting its rich biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palamu Tiger Reserve:**

 
 
• Located in the **Chotanagpur Plateau** region of Jharkhand, it was established in 1974.
 
• The reserve is divided into two divisions: **Betla National Park** and the Palamu Sanctuary.
 
• It is one of the **earliest tiger reserves** to be brought under Project Tiger.
 
 
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched in 1973, it is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at tiger conservation in India.
 
• The program ensures a viable population of tigers while preserving their natural habitats.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity:**
 
 
• Betla National Park is home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, including **medicinal plants, tropical trees, and endangered species**.
 
• The park also hosts several rivers and waterfalls, contributing to its ecological richness.
 
 
 
• **Tourism:**
 
 
• The park offers facilities like jeep safaris and watchtowers for observing wildlife.
 
• Betla National Park is a popular destination for **nature lovers, researchers, and eco-tourists**.

questions.question: Which dynasty did the historian Sirhindi link with the Turkish Caliph?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mughal Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The historian Sirhindi linked the **Mughal Dynasty** with the Turkish Caliphate, emphasizing the Mughal rulers' connection to Islamic authority.
 
• The Mughal emperors, especially Akbar and Aurangzeb, sought religious legitimacy by associating themselves with the Islamic world, including the Turkish Caliph.
 
• This linkage symbolized the Mughals' claim as defenders and promoters of Islam in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Historians like Sirhindi highlighted this connection to reinforce the Islamic identity and authority of the Mughals in a diverse religious and cultural landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Mughal Dynasty ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent from the early 16th to the mid-18th century, with a legacy of art, architecture, and centralized administration.
 
• They were of Turko-Mongol origin and descended from both Genghis Khan (Mongol) and Timur (Turkic).
 
 
 
• **Turkish Caliphate:**
 
 
• The Caliphate was a central Islamic institution that symbolized the unity of the Muslim Ummah (community).
 
• The Ottoman Empire held the Caliphate from the 16th century until its abolition in 1924 by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
 
 
 
• **Role of Religion in Mughal Rule:**
 
 
• Many Mughal rulers, such as Aurangzeb, promoted Islamic law (Sharia) as state policy, while others like Akbar adopted a more inclusive approach through policies like Din-i-Ilahi.
 
• Religious affiliations were often used to consolidate power and gain legitimacy.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of Sirhindi:**
 
 
• Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi (1564–1624) was a prominent Islamic scholar and reformer during the Mughal era.
 
• He emphasized the preservation of Islamic practices and opposed Akbar's syncretic policies like Din-i-Ilahi.

questions.question: The paintings and sculptures of Ajanta Caves in Maharashtra are related to which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ajanta Caves are located in Maharashtra and were built during the period between the 2nd century BCE and the 6th century CE.
 
• The paintings and sculptures found in the Ajanta Caves are primarily related to **Buddhism**, depicting the life and teachings of Gautama Buddha.
 
• The caves are renowned for their intricate frescoes, murals, and carvings, showcasing scenes from the **Jataka tales**, which narrate stories of Buddha's previous lives.
 
• Ajanta Caves served as a monastic retreat for Buddhist monks and were used for meditation, study, and the propagation of Buddhist principles.
 
• The site is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered a masterpiece of ancient Indian art and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhism:**

 
 
• Buddhism is a spiritual tradition founded by Gautama Buddha in the 5th-6th century BCE in India.
 
• It emphasizes the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path to achieve liberation from suffering and attain Nirvana.
 
• The religion spread across Asia and influenced art, culture, and philosophy in regions like China, Japan, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• Jataka tales are a collection of stories about the previous lives of Buddha, illustrating moral and ethical lessons.
 
• These stories are a prominent feature in Buddhist art, including the murals of the Ajanta Caves.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• Ajanta Caves were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• Such sites are recognized for their cultural, historical, or scientific significance and are protected under international conventions.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of Ajanta Caves:**
 
 
• The caves include monasteries (Viharas) and prayer halls (Chaityas), carved into the rock face.
 
• The murals display advanced techniques of shading, perspective, and naturalistic representations of figures.

questions.question: For how many years was the Charter Act of 1793 enacted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Charter Act of 1793 was enacted for **20 years**.
 
• It renewed the charter of the East India Company, allowing them to maintain a monopoly on trade in India for another two decades.
 
• The Act continued the East India Company's rights to govern and administer territories in India.
 
• It also introduced provisions for the appointment of a Governor-General to oversee the administration of British India.
 
• The Charter Act of 1793 laid the groundwork for further legal and administrative reforms in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **East India Company**

 
 
• The East India Company was a British company formed to trade with India and Southeast Asia.
 
• It played a significant role in the colonization and economic exploitation of India during the British rule.
 
• The company controlled vast territories in India, administering them through its officers and administrators.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General of India**
 
 
• The Governor-General was the top British official in India, responsible for overseeing the administration of British territories.
 
• Under the Charter Act of 1793, the Governor-General’s powers were expanded, granting more control over colonial policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Governance**
 
 
• The Charter Act of 1793 was crucial in strengthening the British East India Company's control over Indian territories and its monopoly on trade.
 
• It marked the beginning of a series of Charter Acts that progressively enhanced British colonial authority in India.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Charter Acts**
 
 
• The Charter Act of 1793 was followed by several other Acts, such as the Charter Act of 1813, the Charter Act of 1833, and others, which further extended the East India Company's powers until the company was dissolved in 1874.

questions.question: Which of the following option statements related to the languages and scripts during the Mauryan empire is INCORRECT?

options.text: Most Asokan inscriptions were in the Pali language.
Those in the northwest of the subcontinet were in Aramaic and Greek.
Many Prakrit inscriptions were written in the Brahmi script.
In the northwest, some of them were written in Kharosthi script.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Most Asokan inscriptions were not in the Pali language.** They were predominantly written in Prakrit, which was the common language of the time.
 
• Asoka's inscriptions in the northwest of the subcontinent were indeed written in **Aramaic and Greek scripts**, reflecting the influence of neighboring regions.
 
• Prakrit inscriptions were **written primarily in the Brahmi script**, which became the foundation for many later Indian scripts.
 
• In the northwest of India, some inscriptions were written in **Kharosthi script**, which was influenced by Aramaic script and used for local languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prakrit:** A group of ancient Indo-Aryan languages widely used in India during the Mauryan era. It was the language of the common people and used in official inscriptions.
 
• **Brahmi Script:** The earliest known Indian script, used to write various languages, including Prakrit. It served as the precursor to many modern Indian scripts.
 
• **Kharosthi Script:** A script used mainly in the northwest of India, influenced by Aramaic and suited for writing Prakrit and other regional languages.
 
• **Aramaic and Greek Influence:** The presence of Aramaic and Greek scripts in Asoka’s inscriptions in the northwest indicates cultural and trade exchanges with Hellenistic and Persian regions.
 
• **Asokan Edicts:** These inscriptions were carved on rocks and pillars and were primarily aimed at promoting Dhamma (Buddhist ethics) among the people.

questions.question: When is the International Labour's Day celebrated ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**May 01**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **International Labour Day**, also known as **May Day**, is celebrated globally on **1st May every year**.
 
• It honors the contributions of workers and laborers and commemorates the historic struggles and achievements of the labor movement.
 
• The first celebration of Labour Day was held in **1886 in the United States**, following the Haymarket affair in Chicago.
 
• It is a public holiday in many countries, including India, where it is also referred to as **"Antarrashtriya Shramik Diwas."**
 
• The day symbolizes the importance of workers' rights, fair wages, and better working conditions worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haymarket Affair:**

 
 
• The Haymarket affair occurred on May 4, 1886, in Chicago, where workers protesting for an 8-hour workday faced violent clashes with police.
 
• It played a pivotal role in the establishment of May 1 as International Workers' Day.
 
 
 
• **Labour Day in India:**
 
 
• Labour Day was first celebrated in India on May 1, 1923, in Chennai (then Madras) by the **Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan.**
 
• The day is celebrated to acknowledge the efforts of the working class and promote workers’ rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Workers' Rights:**
 
 
• Workers' rights include fair wages, safe working conditions, the right to unionize, and reasonable working hours.
 
• The International Labour Organization (ILO) plays a critical role in promoting and protecting these rights globally.
 
 
 
• **Labour Movements:**
 
 
• Labour movements have been instrumental in advocating for social and economic reforms for workers worldwide.
 
• Key achievements include the establishment of the 8-hour workday, minimum wages, and workplace safety laws.

questions.question: The Ex-officio secretary of Panchayat Samiti is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Block Development Officer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Block Development Officer (BDO) acts as the **Ex-officio Secretary** of the Panchayat Samiti.
 
• The Panchayat Samiti is the intermediate level of the **three-tier Panchayati Raj system**, established under the **Indian Constitution's Article 243**.
 
• The BDO oversees the implementation of **developmental programs** and ensures administrative efficiency within the block.
 
• As Ex-officio Secretary, the BDO facilitates coordination between the Panchayat Samiti and other government departments for **effective governance.**
 
• The BDO also assists in the preparation and execution of the **block-level budget and development plans.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• It is a decentralized form of government in India where each village is responsible for its own affairs, governed under the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.**
 
• The system consists of three tiers: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
 
 
 
• **Role of Panchayat Samiti:**
 
 
• It is responsible for planning and executing development programs at the block level.
 
• It acts as a link between the Gram Panchayat and the Zilla Parishad.
 
 
 
• **Block Development Officer:**
 
 
• BDO is a government official responsible for development and administrative activities in a block.
 
• They supervise the execution of various state and central government schemes at the block level.
 
 
 
• **Nyay Sachiv:**
 
 
• The Nyay Sachiv (Secretary of Justice) is responsible for legal and judicial matters but does not hold administrative authority over the Panchayat Samiti.

questions.question: In which state is the Onam festival primarily celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Onam** is the most celebrated and significant festival of Kerala, India.
 
• It is a harvest festival that marks the annual homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali.
 
• The festival is celebrated in the month of Chingam (August-September) in the Malayalam calendar.
 
• Onam is a 10-day-long festival featuring cultural events such as **Pookalam** (flower arrangements), **Vallam Kali** (boat races), and **Onasadya** (a traditional feast).
 
• It is considered a symbol of Kerala's rich cultural heritage and unity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Mahabali:**

 
 
• According to mythology, King Mahabali was a generous and just ruler who was sent to the underworld by Lord Vishnu's Vamana avatar.
 
• Onam celebrates his annual visit to his kingdom as a blessing from Lord Vishnu.
 
 
 
• **Onasadya:**
 
 
• Onasadya is a grand vegetarian feast served on banana leaves, consisting of multiple dishes like rice, sambar, avial, and payasam.
 
• It is an integral part of the Onam celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Pookalam:**
 
 
• Pookalam refers to intricate floral designs created on the ground as a form of decoration during Onam.
 
• Each day of the festival sees the addition of more flowers to the Pookalam.
 
 
 
• **Vallam Kali:**
 
 
• Vallam Kali, or snake boat races, are thrilling events held during Onam in Kerala's backwaters.
 
• It attracts huge crowds and showcases teamwork and traditional boat-building skills.
 
 
 
• **Unity in Diversity:**
 
 
• Onam is celebrated by people of all religions and communities in Kerala, reflecting the state's unity and harmony.
 
• It is a festival that transcends cultural and religious boundaries.
